avis.comment: Purely theoretical paper. Problem statement keeps to background and prior work and poses open questions without revealing entry-wise separability or the theorems. Classification theory_only / not_applicable / [] is correct. All quotes match the text; C3 overreaches by asking the criterion to distinguish architectures the paper explicitly does not characterize. Null compute is appropriate.

targets.comment: Quote is exact (Prior Work 1); the paper recasts Pinkus in its framework and claims to encompass prior settings, so a special-case recovery check is a reasonable sanity control.
Quote exact (Remark 1); recovering Segol-Lipman and WL-type results as special cases is what the paper does and a natural control for any general account.

Quote exact and the counterexamples exist, but the target asks that the criterion distinguish U(C,I) from U(P,I); the paper does not do this (separation cannot, Remark 2 says these need differential operators) and instead sidesteps them by adding a readout.
Quote exact (Example 3); testing a proposed separation notion on stacks of width-1 convolutions under S_n is a concrete, checkable sanity case supported by the paper.
Quote exact (contributions list); core invariant result (Theorem 1).
Quote exact (Introduction); entry-wise separation via projections onto output coordinates is the paper's key concept.
Quote exact (Introduction); matches Theorems 2 and 3 (depth stabilization or width-1 convolutional output layer).
Quote exact (Abstract); Example 3 shows global separation fails to characterize equivariant universality classes.
Quote exact (Related Work); failure is from cited prior work, restated in Prior Work 1 item 6 and echoed by Example 3, so acceptable; overlaps with C3 and S1.
